declaredStatus.claim: Shared browser-renderer workbench receives explicit runtime capabilities, owns cross-view async orchestration and must preserve source lifecycle and controlled UI contracts.
declaredStatus.evidenceLimit: This report checks shared source/session composition only and does not accept either production transport/runtime.

checks.question: Is the inspected composition owned by the shared workbench without runtime or specialist implementation imports?
checks.detail: All six internal production dependencies use workspace:*. A TypeScript runtime-import scan of 68 workbench source files finds no app, Node, GM/Tauri/Electron or tag/creation/source implementation imports in the tested import allowlist. The inspected orchestration calls injected source/session capabilities and supplies controlled props/events. SFC and external-package transitive graphs were not exhaustively scanned.

checks.question: Are source/session capabilities explicitly injected and the root entry separated from renderer feature execution?
checks.detail: The runtime contract injects sources, HTTP/storage/login/media and optional native capabilities. The local root runtime graph reaches four workbench files with no eager Vue/Pinia/codec/source implementation edge; external package internals and production artifacts are not accepted. Probe request counters show one session call per explicit source selection and a second call on explicit retry. Source implementation dynamic-import retry is deferred to B10.

checks.question: Does selecting a source maintain identity ownership through pending, failure, retry, invalidation and disposal?
checks.detail: B05-M01 fails: refresh starts the new request without clearing or replacing the displayed session when its source identity changes. Node rendering confirms the new selection still projects source A username and signed-in status until source B completes. Five controls pass: same-source refresh preserves identity, switching back suppresses late B publication, operational failure supports explicit retry, invalidation withdraws identity, and scope disposal suppresses completion. The probe reproduces the real source-ID watcher connection rather than mounting the full workbench or testing native cancellation.

checks.question: Do inspected session failures use serializable errors and retain per-source cache ownership?
checks.detail: Failure is normalized with toAppErrorState; the retry probe retains network-error and moves to signed-out after retry. Settled session cache entries are keyed by source ID; stale completion/invalidation/disposal do not publish new entries. This does not inspect stable snapshots, native credentials or storage isolation (B06/B12), and does not negate the transient displayed-identity defect in C3.

checks.question: Are tests owned correctly and findings bounded by current reproducible evidence?
checks.detail: The 104 existing targeted tests in 11 files and workbench typecheck pass. Six supplemental behavioral scenarios produce five passes and one confirmed failure. UI source-contract tests do not prove layout, and Node SSR does not prove browser behavior. The temporary probe was copied to local evidence storage and removed; all 17 hashed inputs and the product working tree remain unchanged.

static.detail: Import scan passes. Source review plus the behavioral reproduction establish the identity projection failure.

findings.title: Switching sources temporarily displays the previous source account identity
findings.trigger: A has a settled signed-in session. Select B with session capability while B.getSession() remains pending. Observe the controlled session badge without an overriding accountLabel, as in the Userscript composition.
findings.effect: The selected source/account controls refer to B while session state and the rendered username still belong to A. This is transient incorrect account/login presentation; no native grant, credential exposure or cross-account request has been demonstrated.
findings.suggestedNextAction: Track which source owns the displayed session. On a source change, show that source cached session or checking before starting its refresh. Preserve known identity for same-source refresh, retain generation/error/invalidation/disposal behavior and add a permanent regression test. Keep the controlled badge presentation rule unchanged unless a separate requirement is established.
